question: How many buttons may the right hand panel keep?
context: The placement contract says the panel shows what the picked thing is, as label and value rows. Today about forty one-shot buttons sit in it. Pro editors differ: Final Cut's inspector has almost none, Photoshop's Properties panel keeps a few quick actions.

options.label: One main action per section
options.summary: Each section keeps at most one button, the action the section exists for (Add Captions in an empty Captions section, Normalize on a sound, Key it). Everything else you do once moves to right-click and the menu bar.
pros: Like Photoshop's Properties panel, which keeps a few quick actions
The obvious next step is still where your eye already is
Most of today's rows of buttons go away
cons: A judgment call per section on which action is the main one
options.mitigation: The contract names the rule (the action the section exists for) so each section answers it the same way.

options.label: No buttons at all
options.summary: The panel holds only label and value rows, plus the + that adds to a list. Every action lives on right-click and in the menu bar.
pros: The strictest reading of one purpose per area
cons: A first timer looking at an empty Captions section has no visible way to add captions
Further from Photoshop and Premiere, which both keep a few panel buttons
options.mitigation: An empty section could show one short label pointing at the right-click, but that is a sentence in the panel.

options.label: Leave the panel as it is
options.summary: Keep every button where it is today. The actions also get menu rows through the menu bar task.
pros: Nothing moves that people have learned
cons: The panel keeps mixing things you tune with things you do once, which is what the placement contract is against
